A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Matching relocated material supports comparison; inconsistencies in particular captions are addressed below.

before.justification: V3 reports original representation analyses, pruning evaluations, and concept-steering experiments, including the ECG5000 case study in Appendix F.

after.justification: V4 retains original pruning and steering results in the main text and Appendices F–G, including numerical benchmark results and the ECG5000 experiment.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the prescribed pruning operation from zeroing intermediate-layer weights to removing those layers and skipping computation. Block selection and boundary preservation remain unchanged. Appendix C still partly describes zeroing, leaving the implementation underlying the retained results unclear.

E1.justification: Benchmark datasets and ECG5000 are retained. However, v4 Figure 14 replaces v3 Figure 18's trend, periodicity, and amplitude contrasts with constant or sinusoidal versus trend contrasts, while retaining incompatible panel names and discussion. Whether the underlying concept tasks changed is unresolved.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same unpruned models, pruning configurations, and external comparators. These include TS2Vec and T-Loss in Table 11 and AnomalyTransformer, DGHL, GPT4TS, and TimesNet in Table 9. Newly cited dataset sources do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Stated benchmark protocols remain unchanged, including masking rates, metrics, and forecasting horizons. Table 6 retains three training epochs, batch size 64, and learning rate 0.0001; Table 7 retains 100 timing passes using length-512 inputs. The new seed disclosure does not establish a changed evaluation design.

E4.justification: V4 newly reports a qualitative steering robustness check across multiple random seeds and revises the localization heatmaps. Existing mean-versus-median and single-versus-multiple-token ablations, steering-strength guidance, and the ECG5000 case study are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Section 4 first states that steering datasets were generated using multiple random seeds, without specifying their number or reporting per-seed uncertainty. This does not establish an increase in runs. Five-seed imputation statistics and timing standard deviations were already reported in v3.

E6.justification: Numerical tables remain unchanged, but localization heatmaps and their overlaid curves change in Figures 7 and 14, with ambiguous task correspondence. V4 also adds a seed-consistency finding and an unsupported claim of up to 52% inference speedup: unchanged Table 7 reports 52.70% model sparsity, while MOMENT's all-block timing changes from 20.88 to 19.82 ms.

T1.justification: The CKA, Fisher criterion, LDR, cosine-similarity, and SVCCA equations remain unchanged, as do the synthetic-data and redundant-block definitions. Neither version adds distinct theorem or proof content.

C1.justification: The abstract and three headline contributions retain their scope: representation redundancy supports pruning, linear concepts can be identified and localized, and latent interventions steer predictions without additional training. Reframing steering as applying conceptual priors preserves these core claims.

C2.justification: V4 interprets the retained ECG experiment and new seed statement as evidence of robustness across synthetic and real data, and adds financial-event applications. It removes v3's explicit limitations concerning complex patterns and transferring synthetic steering matrices to out-of-distribution real series, while retaining future architectural and task extensions.

D1.justification: The Reproducibility Statement replaces the anonymous code snapshot link with a project GitHub link and removes the promised future release of synthetic datasets and pruned models. Hardware and model specifications remain unchanged. Figure 8 newly explains the displayed raw predictions and moving averages.

R1.justification: V4 adds four dataset-source references: Dau, Godahewa, Keogh, and Paparrizos and colleagues. Section 3.1 also explicitly distinguishes boundary-preserving block pruning from Nguyen et al.'s individual-layer pruning. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata for retained works.

P1.justification: V4 locally rewrites the pruning explanation, steering discussion, limitations, and reproducibility statement, expands acknowledgments, and separates supplementary steering and pruning into Appendices F and G. The main section sequence and most methodological prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Central visual presentations are substantially reorganized: Figure 3 is redrawn, Figure 7 changes from three panels to one enlarged plot, and Figure 8 contracts from nine steering panels to six. Separate appendix compositional-steering figures become a paired MOMENT/Chronos grid; localization plots are reformatted and relocated, and Table 8 moves.

improvement.justification: V4 improves figure organization, clarifies steering captions, and updates code-access instructions. However, its new 52% speedup claim is unsupported by unchanged Table 7, revised localization figures have inconsistent concept labels, and specific synthetic-to-real transfer limitations disappear. These reporting regressions outweigh the presentation gains, while the retained benchmark evidence limits the deterioration's extent.
